article_title: Cloudflare Traces Enters Open Beta With OTLP Export, and Observability Pricing Changes on December 1

content_preview.title: Cloudflare Traces Enters Open Beta With OTLP Export, and Observability Pricing Changes on December 1
content_preview.summary: Cloudflare Traces records spans for security rules, caching, routing, Workers and origin handling. New volume-based observability pricing starts December 1, 2026.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Cloudflare has introduced Cloudflare Traces in open beta, extending automatic tracing beyond Workers to the rest of the request path, [according to the Cloudflare Blog](https://blog.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-tracing/). The company says the service is available from the dashboard, through the API, or with Terraform, and can export to an OTLP destination. editor_notes.content_quality: Clear News structure (Overview, What Traces Does, Sampling/Trace Rules/Propagation, Pricing, What We Don't Know, Analysis). 755 words, within the 400-1200 News range. Includes a clear list of unknowns and no AI self-reference.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read both gzipped snapshots from disk (gunzip, HTML to text) for sources/2026-10/cloudflare-traces-enters-open-beta-with-otlp-export-and-observability-pricing-changes-on-december-1/. source-0.html.gz (blog.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-tracing/, 200, dated October 2, 2026; full body present, not a JS shell, so the bot's raw-HTML download held): confirms open beta; automatic tracing beyond Workers; dashboard/API/Terraform availability with OTLP export; verbatim quote 'records each supported step as a span, including its timing, outcome, and relevant attributes'; no special instrumentation/config/plugins; 527ms of 539ms cache-miss example; Workers Tracing launched last year; baseline sampling with '1% of requests' as an example ('might trace'); Trace Rules overriding to 100% for hostname/source IP/header with same Rules language (paths, methods, headers, IPs, geographies); W3C traceparent accept and forward to origin with incoming propagation policy; account-level OTLP destination then per-domain selection; Observability MCP server + SQL API; roadmap (DDoS rules, Access, Workflows, Queues, Pipelines, authenticated propagation, ad hoc tracing, OTel API in Workers, up to 365 days retention); pricing table: Free 0.5 GB ingestion per day, 7 days, additional not available; Paid and Enterprise 50 GB ingestion and 10 GB-month storage per billing cycle, up to 1 year (coming soon), $0.25 per GB ingested and $0.10 per GB-month stored; new pricing effective across Cloudflare Tracing and Workers Tracing starting December 1, 2026; pricing based on ingested/retained data rather than number of spans/events. All match the article verbatim. source-1.html.gz (blog.cloudflare.com/one-observability-platform/, 200, October 2, 2026): confirms same pricing table; 'Beginning December 1, 2026, this pricing model will apply across all plans (effective upon renewal for all Enterprise customers) and cover existing Developer Platform logs, including Workers, Containers, AI Gateway, as well as all tracing data'; 'Logpush, previously available only to Enterprise, is now available on all self-serve plans'; Logpush table 25 GB included, $0.03 per GB to Cloudflare destinations, $0.10 per GB to external destinations; '30 days of domain analytics on every plan'. All match. Pricing direction: neither source characterizes the change as a cut or a rise (the vendor frames it as 'simpler and more predictable'; one sentence in source-1, 'This pricing adjustment will be.', is truncated). The article correctly describes it only as a shift to volume-based billing, attributes it to Cloudflare, and states in What We Don't Know that the effect on existing users is unstated. Manifest: both sources status 200, suspicious_patterns null for both, so nothing to adjudicate. blog.cloudflare.com is on the allowlist. No snapshot failed; no WebFetch used.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every price, tier, allowance, unit, date and feature claim traces to the snapshots. All vendor claims are attributed to Cloudflare ('according to the Cloudflare Blog', 'Cloudflare says', 'per ... companion announcement'). The Analysis sentence (accounts with sizable logs will be billed by ingested and stored gigabytes from December 1, 2026) is a reasonable, non-evaluative restatement. Minor imprecision: the summary of 'Paid and Enterprise' omits that Enterprise applies on renewal, but the body covers this explicitly.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional; no promotional language. Pricing described neither as a cut nor a rise.
editor_notes.originality: Checked 2026-10 articles. The Cloudflare Basin article (05) cites The Register and developers.cloudflare.com Basin docs and does not mention observability or tracing; the Worker Previews article (2026-09/30) is a different product; vinext (10-02) unrelated. Neither source URL appears in any other content file. No overlap.
concerns: Both sources are vendor posts, with no independent coverage or user verification; the article attributes claims to Cloudflare throughout, so this is acceptable for a launch/pricing announcement.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, well-attributed News article. All prices, tiers, dates and features verified against the stored snapshots. APPROVE.
